name: Aphaurosuchus
sum: Aphaurosuchus is an extinct baurusuchid crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous Bauru Basin of southern Brazil.
wsnote: No body-length estimate is given in the sources consulted.
holotype: LPRP/USP 0697, a nearly complete skeleton broken into six main blocks (Fazenda Furnas site, Jales, São Paulo; Adamantina/Vale do Rio do Peixe Formation).
material: The nearly complete holotype skeleton, two isolated caudal vertebrae with osteoderms and rib fragments; A. kaiju is based on fragmentary skull remains including parts of the mandible, palate and teeth.
biology: The sources consulted describe its anatomy and naming only; they give no direct evidence of diet or habits.
author: Darlim et al. 2021

sources.text: Darlim, Gustavo; Montefeltro, Felipe C.; Langer, Max C. 2021. 3D skull modelling and description of a new baurusuchid (Crocodyliformes, Mesoeucrocodylia) from the Late Cretaceous (Bauru Basin) of Brazil. Journal of Anatomy 239(3): 622–662. doi:10.1111/joa.13442
